intro: To add slide numbers in PowerPoint on Mac, click Insert > Header & Footer, tick Slide number on the Slide tab, and click Apply to All. That numbers every slide in the deck, and one more tick keeps the title slide clean.
tldr: Go to Insert > Header & Footer, tick Slide number on the Slide tab, then click Apply to All.
Apply to All numbers every slide, including hidden ones. Hidden slides still take a value in the count.
Tick Don't show on title slide if the cover should stay clean.
Starting at a value other than one has two possible routes, so test them on a copy first.
If numbers vanish, check the Slide Master and the layout each slide uses.

blocks.text: Slide numbers help people find their place in a long deck. They also give a room a fixed reference when someone asks about one specific page during a meeting. PowerPoint handles numbering through the same footer tools it uses for dates and footer text. This guide starts with the Mac steps, then covers the edge cases that trip people up: title slides, hidden slides, starting values and numbers that vanish.
Which PowerPoint for Mac you have

Microsoft's Mac help page for this task names three versions: PowerPoint for Microsoft 365 for Mac, PowerPoint 2024 for Mac and PowerPoint 2021 for Mac. The menu names match across all three, so the steps in this guide apply to each. The page shows no publication date, only a 2026 copyright line. Treat it as current guidance, and check it against the menus on your own screen.

items: Open the deck in PowerPoint for Mac, not in a browser, unless you use the web steps further down.
Decide which slides need a number and which should stay clean before you change anything.
Work on a copy if colleagues share the file, because master edits reach every slide that uses them.
Look under the PowerPoint menu to confirm your version, so you know which guide matches your screen.

blocks.text: Add slide numbers to every slide

The main route runs through the Header and Footer box. Choose Insert > Header & Footer, and the box opens. On the Slide tab, the Slide number check box adds the number to each slide. Apply to All writes that setting across the deck, so you never need to select slides first. This is the route Microsoft documents for PowerPoint for Mac.
Add footer text and dates in the same box

The same box handles more than numbers. Microsoft's Mac page covers the date, the time and footer text in one place. Type footer text in the footer field on the Slide tab, then click Apply to All. A confidentiality line or a department name works well there. Keep the footer short so it does not crowd the slide number.
Hide the number on the title slide

Most decks look cleaner without a number on the cover. Select Don't show on title slide before you click Apply to All. If the cover is missing its number and you want one, clear that box and apply again. Microsoft's Mac page says that box must be cleared for numbers to appear on the title slide.
Hidden slides and manual numbers

PowerPoint counts every slide when it numbers the deck, including hidden slides. A hidden slide still takes its place in the count, so the next visible slide can look like it skipped one. Microsoft's Mac page says the way to exclude hidden slides is to number each visible slide by hand with a text box. That works for a short deck. It becomes fragile once you reorder slides.

To number by hand, insert a text box on each visible slide and type the value. Put the box in the same corner on every slide so the numbers line up. Manual boxes do not update when slides move, so check each one after you reorder the deck.
Change the starting number

Starting at a value other than one is the least settled part of this topic. A 2022 Microsoft Q&A answer from the community says the Header and Footer box has a Start at box where you type the first number. Microsoft's cross-platform support page gives another route: Design > Slide Size > Custom Slide Size, then Number slides from, then OK. That page covers Windows, Mac and the web together, so it does not say which steps belong to which platform.

Test either route on a copy of your deck before you rely on it. Set the starting value, then check the first visible slide and the one after it. If the number does not change, try the other route. This guide did not confirm either route in a live copy of PowerPoint for Mac.
Apply numbers to selected slides

Microsoft's cross-platform page says Apply to All covers every slide, while Apply affects only the currently selected slide. Microsoft's Mac page mentions only Apply to All. So a one-slide Apply on a Mac is not confirmed in Microsoft's Mac help. If only some slides need numbers, add text boxes to those slides instead.
Move and style slide numbers on the Slide Master

Numbers sit in a placeholder on the slide master, so you style them there. Choose View > Slide Master. Select the page number placeholder, then press and hold it until the four-headed arrow appears. Drag it to its new position, then select Close Master View. Changes to the master carry through to layouts that use that placeholder.

Font, size and color changes work the same way. Select the placeholder, then change its text formatting in the ribbon. Check the result on dark slides too, since a gray number on a black background can vanish.
Why slide numbers don't show up

Missing numbers usually come from one of three causes. The layout may lack a slide number placeholder. The slide master may have had that placeholder removed. Or a shape may sit over the number. Microsoft Q&A threads from 2023 on macOS list the same causes, and the accepted fix starts with the Header & Footer route you already tried.

items: Open View > Slide Master and check the top master and each child layout for a slide number placeholder.
Switch any slide that uses a layout without that placeholder to a layout that has one.
Move any picture, text box or shape that covers the number.
Clear Don't show on title slide if the number is missing only from the cover.

blocks.text: Page Setup is a different menu

Microsoft's Mac Page Setup article describes another route: File > Page Setup, then Header/Footer. The article says this is where you add the date, time, slide numbers or footer text. It does not cover a starting number. Use Insert > Header & Footer for most work, and treat Page Setup as the documented alternative.
Use the web version instead

If you work in PowerPoint for the web in a browser, the route is Insert > Footer > Slide Number. A Footer pane opens. Tick Slide number, optionally tick Don't show on title slide, then click Apply to All. Use Apply to Selected Slides when only some slides should change. Microsoft's web page lists no start-number option and no Header & Footer dialog.
Common mistakes

items: Adding a number to one slide and expecting the rest to follow. Apply to All is the setting that covers the whole deck.
Typing numbers by hand on every slide, then reordering the deck and forgetting to update them.
Forgetting that hidden slides still take a place in the count.
Editing one slide's placeholder when the fix belongs on the Slide Master.
Searching for a keyboard shortcut. No Mac shortcut for this task appears on Microsoft's pages, so use the menus.

blocks.text: Check the release notes before you trust an old guide

Older guides can show menus that have since moved. The 2022 Q&A thread was written for Mac version 16.67, and the app has had many builds since then. Microsoft's release notes list PowerPoint for Mac 16.114.3, built October 27, 2026, with labels such as quality and performance improvements. The part of that page we read showed no entry about headers, footers, slide numbers or the Slide Master. That read covered only the first 100,000 of 132,703 characters, so treat it as a partial check.
What to do next

Once the numbers look right, play the deck in Slide Show view from the first slide to the last. Check the cover, any section breaks and every hidden slide. Save a copy before you share it. If you plan to add speaker notes or record narration next, follow [how to add speaker notes in PowerPoint on Mac](/how-to/add-speaker-notes-in-powerpoint) or [how to record a slide show in PowerPoint on Mac](/how-to/record-a-slide-show-in-powerpoint).

faq.question: Does Apply to All number hidden slides too?
faq.answer: Yes. PowerPoint counts every slide, including hidden ones. Microsoft's Mac page says that excluding hidden slides means numbering each visible slide by hand with a text box.

faq.question: Why is my title slide missing its number?
faq.answer: Most likely Don't show on title slide is selected in the Header and Footer box. Clear that check box, then click Apply to All again.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut for slide numbers on Mac?
faq.answer: Not one that Microsoft documents for this task. Use Insert > Header & Footer, tick Slide number on the Slide tab, then click Apply to All.

faq.question: Can I start my slide numbers at a value other than one?
faq.answer: Possibly, but the location of the setting is not settled. Look for a Start at box in the Header and Footer box, or use Design > Slide Size > Custom Slide Size > Number slides from. Test on a copy first.

faq.question: How do I number just one slide?
faq.answer: Microsoft's Mac page documents only Apply to All. For one slide, add a text box with the number. That route is the safe one.

faq.question: Can I move the slide number to another corner?
faq.answer: Yes. Choose View > Slide Master, press and hold the page number placeholder until the four-headed arrow appears, drag it, then select Close Master View.

faq.question: Does PowerPoint for the web work the same way?
faq.answer: Mostly. Choose Insert > Footer > Slide Number, tick Slide number in the Footer pane, then click Apply to All. Microsoft's web page lists no start-number option.

task: Add slide numbers to every slide in PowerPoint for Mac
appliesTo: PowerPoint for Microsoft 365 for Mac, PowerPoint 2024 for Mac and PowerPoint 2021 for Mac
requirements: PowerPoint for Microsoft 365 for Mac, PowerPoint 2024 for Mac or PowerPoint 2021 for Mac
The deck open in PowerPoint for Mac, or in PowerPoint for the web if you use the web steps
No Mac keyboard shortcut is documented for this task, so the steps use menus

steps.name: Open the deck
steps.text: Open the presentation in PowerPoint for Mac. Work in normal editing view so the slide thumbnails appear in the left pane.

steps.name: Open the Insert tab
steps.text: Click the Insert tab in the ribbon at the top of the PowerPoint window. The header and footer tools live on this tab.

steps.name: Click Header & Footer
steps.text: On the Insert tab, click Header & Footer. The Header and Footer box opens over the deck.
steps.tip: If you cannot find the button, ask Lazur to point at it, as described in the box further down.

steps.name: Select the Slide tab
steps.text: In the Header and Footer box, click the Slide tab. Slide numbers are set on this tab.

steps.name: Tick Slide number
steps.text: Select the Slide number check box. Optional: select Don't show on title slide to keep the number off the opening slide.
steps.tip: Leave the title slide box clear if the cover should carry a number.

steps.name: Click Apply to All
steps.text: Click Apply to All. PowerPoint writes the setting to every slide in the deck, including any slides you hide later.

steps.name: Check the slides
steps.text: Scroll the slide thumbnails and confirm each visible slide shows its number. If one does not, use the troubleshooting list below.

troubleshooting.problem: Numbers don't appear on the title slide
troubleshooting.fix: Open Insert > Header & Footer, clear Don't show on title slide on the Slide tab, then click Apply to All again.

troubleshooting.problem: Numbers are missing from some slides
troubleshooting.fix: Check View > Slide Master for a slide number placeholder on the top master and each child layout. Switch affected slides to a layout that has one, and move any shape covering the number.

troubleshooting.problem: Numbers skip a value after a hidden slide
troubleshooting.fix: PowerPoint numbers hidden slides too. To skip them, number each visible slide with a text box, and retype those boxes after you reorder the deck.

troubleshooting.problem: Numbers start at one and you need another start
troubleshooting.fix: Look for a Start at box in the Header and Footer box, or try Design > Slide Size > Custom Slide Size > Number slides from. Test the route on a copy first.

troubleshooting.problem: The slide number is hard to see
troubleshooting.fix: Open View > Slide Master, select the page number placeholder, and change its color, size or font. Then select Close Master View.
